It would probably be more accurate to say "all relevant chassis status properties".

Present and Enabled, for example, are not directly related to chassis power.
If you are going to mention a class, you should probably specify the class name (ChassisStatusMonitor) rather than the phrase "chassis status monitor".

Usually the Tested: line is following by a brief bullet list of tests.

```
Tested:
- Verified all monitored ...
- Verified invalid chassis ...
```
can you show example output here?

The purpose of this struct is to configure which properties are monitored.

The default value for all of the struct fields is "false", meaning that property not monitored.

If you try to get the value of an unmonitored property, some return a logical default and others throw an exception. See the doxygen for details. But you aren't getting the real value for any of the properties if monitoring is not enabled.

In your case, I think you want to turn on all monitoring. Set all struct fields to true.

The first chassis is 1, not 0. The last chassis number is dependent on the system type. Some systems might have 1, 4, 8, or 12.

For now you could just let the ChassisStatusMonitor class throw exceptions if they specify an invalid chassis number.
In the documentation chassis 0 was called out as the "global system designation for all sleds", which is why I started there.

You probably don't want to call this twice. I'd suggest putting the value in a local as a result of the first call to std::atoi.

Note you can also have CLI verify an option value and print a command line parsing error if the chassis number was not valid (<1, not an integer, etc.)

The D-Bus chassis path is specific to the chassis. So for chassis 2 it will be `/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis2`.

You could use `std::format("/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis{}", chassisNumber);`

You might want to print
```
Chassis 2
```

at the top.

Then for each property print the property name + a colon before the try catch. Then in the catch you can print something like "Unknown" as the value with the exception error message indented on a line below?

e.g.

```
Chassis 2
  Present: true
  Available: unknown
    Error: Property does not exist
  Enabled: false
  ...
```
Is this for future expansion? I don't see it getting set anywhere.
I had brought it in from an example I used. I will remove it.
Chassis status tool. You can probably delete the "for OpenBMC" part, since all the code in this repo is for OpenBMC.
I wouldn't mind it dumping every chassis by default, and then if you add a chassis arg it would only do that one.

If you take Matt's suggestion and have the default behavior be dump all chassis, then perhaps this becomes an option with no argument?

Then there is a separate option (-c or -n or something) for the "chassis number"?

Regardless, you need to specify in the command help that the user should specify a chassis number from 1 to N, where N is the number of chassis.

You might consider using the add_subcommand() method so that the command looks like `chassis-status-tool dump` rather than `chassis-status-tool -d`. A lot of the tools we use, like git/systemctl/busctl, have the pattern of a subcommand with options specific to it.  See phosphor-fan-presence/control/fanctl.cpp for an example.
I think "Dump chassis status" would be more clear.
Do you need a try/catch around the parse? Not sure if CLI throws if an invalid option is specified.

No, invalid options will throw an error message to the console "The following argument was not expected: -arg
Run with --help for more information". A try catch is also not used around CLI11_PARSE in the other tools or apps in the phosphor power library.
I don't understand the usage of this variable. Did it previously contain a large returned string from dump(), and now it is just empty?
I had brought it in from an example I used. I will remove it.
I don't think this works correctly?

Could you remove the " Requested" part?

You are 100% correct. That is the true meaning of the property value.

However, I think people will be confused. The reason is that even after a successful power on/off, it will still look like it was requested and has not yet completed. So we can probably avoid some future questions by making the description a little less accurate 😊

If this is just a chassis number now (which I think is good), the variable name should probably be chassisNumber.

Also, I think if you declare that local as an int, then CLI will give an error for non-ints and convert it for you.

See comment above re: variable name and conversion.

If you decide to keep a string value initially, the new local should be chassisNumber. The OpenBMC coding convention is to use camelCase rather than snake_case for variables/functions/etc. It is a bit confusing since the standard libraries use snake_case, but we need to follow the convention.

Good point. To be consistent with the other files in this repo you should probably copy the comment block at the top of one of the existing files (like phosphor-power-sequencer/src/chassis.cpp). The year in the comment should be 2026 as it is the creation date.
adding blank lines to logically separate parts is usually a good idea, though if Shawn was OK then I am.
Good point. This would be more readable if there was a blank line between the block that handles each property. Matt meant blank lines in the source code, not the tool output.
Had it in for a function when I first start this story, will remove.
